newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Nestle declines comment on Australia coffee prices.
newsitem.headline: Nestle declines comment on Australia coffee prices.

text.p: Swiss-owned Nestle Australia Ltd declined to comment on Friday on any plans by the company to raise domestic retail prices after a surge in international prices to around 20-year highs.

Nestle last raised its Australian instant coffee prices 10 percent in April, which restored the product to the same levels it had been a year previously before the firm lowered prices by the same amount, spokesman Peter Kelly told Reuters.
Kelly said April's increase represented only a fraction of the 100 percent rise in the price of coffee beans over the same period.
Nestle holds 70 percent of Australia's instant coffee market and has 54 percent of the country's total coffee market by volume.

World coffee prices soared to 20-year highs on the New York futures market on Thursday on frantic buying from speculators and commercial coffee firms worried about small coffee stockpiles and shrinking crop prospects.
Some managers of coffee bars on Sydney's streets said they expected surging world prices to be passed through to their customers in coming weeks.
"We haven't raised our prices yet, but we've been told by our supplier that its coming in a month or two," John Louicv, manager of the Euro cafe in Sydney's business district.
Louicv said a cup of capuccino currently retails for about A$2.50 in Sydney's trendiest cafes, although that could change with higher wholesale prices on the cards.
"It's inevitable," said another cafe manager. "If prices go up around the world, its got to hit us at some point."
Richard Palm of Angco Ltd, which imports coffee into Australia from Papua New Guinea, said he has seen his costs more than double recently.
"Two months ago I paid US$40,000 for a cargo of coffee (18 tonnes)," Palm said. "That same cargo now costs US$90,120."
